text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for gptq-4-small on /chat/stream. Dashboard shows ~7% -> ~2% between 03:00-03:20 UTC. :thinking:

maria: Oh no. Do we have per-customer slices? could be one tenant invalidating keys (template change?) :eyes:

kevin: I pulled perf traces. There's a surge of requests with slightly different prompt normalization (we trimmed trailing punctuation in the prompt_normalizer PR last week). That would change cache keying.

lucy: Query I used in Datadog (rough):
```
avg:last_1h:prefix_cache.hit_rate{model:gptq-4-small,route:chat_stream}.rollup(avg,3600)
```
Got a drop timed with the PR rollout window. Also checked token_savings metric: token_savings_per_min down ~60%.

alex: Is there evidence of key collisions or a bug in the keying function? Could also be KV store warmup behavior if we restarted nodes.

kevin: Not collisions — looks like key entropy increased (different normalized prompts produce distinct keys). Warmup might be involved too: a subtle interaction where we prepopulate only exact prior keys. If many slightly-different keys appear, warmup isn't effective.

maria: Proposed mitigation: fallback to older normalizer for the canary customers and run an A/B to measure hit-rate restoration. Also add an alert for >40% drop in token_savings over 30m per-customer slice.

lucy: Dashboard changes I recommend:
- add per-customer heatmap (hit_rate by customer, last_24h)
- show top-50 changed cache keys (hash prefix) to inspect variance
- per-route and per-model token_savings trend lines

kevin: Quick notes on instrumentation to add:
```
# prometheus-ish pseudo
prefix_cache.key_entropy{model="$model",route="$route",customer="$cust"}
prefix_cache.hit_rate{...}
prefix_cache.warmup_misses_total{...}
```
Expose key_entropy so we can see when normalization increases uniqueness.

perf-bot: Created incident PERF-2026-57: prefix-cache hit-rate drop (gptq-4-small /chat/stream). Linked runbook: <https://runbook.internal/redwood/prefix-cache-drops> :warning:

alex: Action items:
1) kevin rollback normalization for 2 canary customers (low-traffic) + monitor hit_rate + token_savings (ETA ~30m).
2) lucy add per-customer heatmap + key_entropy panel to eng-runtime dashboard.
3) maria add datadog alert for token_savings drop and a short postmortem checklist.

maria: I'll own the PM side for communication with affected customers. If rollback restores hit-rate, we consider a more gradual migration with compatibility layer.

kevin: starting rollback on canary customers now. will post results in ~20m. :thumbsup:

lucy: I'll sketch dashboard panels and push a dashboard change after rollback check.

alex: Thanks everyone — please paste final numbers (hit_rate, token_savings) here when you have them so we can close the incident.

perf-bot: Incident PERF-2026-57 updated: rollback in progress by kevin.
